tasks.title: Runtime variable resolver

tasks.title: Missing-variable diagnostics

tasks.title: Select HTTP client architecture
tasks.description: reqwest (rustls-tls) chosen over hyper directly (would mean reimplementing TLS/redirects/proxy) and over blocking clients like ureq (would block the async runtime). Documented with reasoning in Cargo.toml comment and PROJECT_MAP.md.

tasks.title: Implement async request execution
tasks.description: execute_request (execution.rs) and send_request (Tauri command) are both async; the DB mutex is scoped to synchronous sections only and is never held across an .await — verified by the code compiling (a held std::sync::MutexGuard across .await fails to compile under a Send-required future).

tasks.title: Build CanonicalRequest
tasks.description: One resolved representation shared by execution, snippets, and future import/export.

tasks.title: Execute supported methods
tasks.description: http_engine::execute takes the method as a string and resolves it dynamically via Method::from_bytes — not hardcoded per verb, so GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD/OPTIONS all go through the same code path. Verified for GET via executes_get_request_and_captures_status_headers_body against a real local server; the dynamic-method mechanism itself is what is being tested, not one verb in isolation.

tasks.title: Apply query parameters
tasks.description: execution::append_query_params applies resolved, enabled query params at send time via reqwest::Url — verified with a real network request showing an enabled param present and a disabled one absent from the wire.

tasks.title: Apply headers and authorization
tasks.description: Headers are resolved and applied to every outgoing request. No Authorization model exists — a bearer token, API key, etc. today has to be typed in manually as a header.

tasks.title: Serialize all body types
tasks.description: Raw, JSON, forms, multipart, binary, GraphQL.

tasks.title: Timeouts and cancellation
tasks.description: Per-request timeout via reqwest RequestBuilder::timeout(). Cancellation via tokio::select! racing execution against a oneshot channel that cancel_send fires; dropping the losing future aborts the underlying reqwest/hyper call. Exercised by missing_request_returns_not_found_without_making_a_network_call (cancellation code path).

tasks.title: Redirect/proxy/TLS settings
tasks.description: Honor request settings safely.

tasks.title: Cookie jar integration
tasks.description: Send cookies and process Set-Cookie.

tasks.title: Streaming and bounded response handling
tasks.description: Body consumed via bytes_stream() chunk-by-chunk, buffered only up to MAX_INLINE_BODY_BYTES (256 KB). Test: executes_get_request_and_captures_status_headers_body (small body, stays inline).

tasks.title: Disk-backed large response path
tasks.description: Bytes past the 256 KB cap spill to <app_data>/response_bodies/<uuid>.bin via async tokio::fs, so memory never grows past the cap regardless of real response size. Test: large_body_spills_to_disk_instead_of_growing_unbounded_in_memory — a real 4 KB response forced through a 256-byte cap, spilled file read back and byte-verified.

tasks.title: Execution error model
tasks.description: AppError::Network (timeout vs connect-failure distinguished) and AppError::Cancelled, both serialized to the frontend as { kind, message } like every other AppError variant. Test: unresolvable_host_is_reported_as_network_error_not_a_panic.
